en.title: Maximum Layered XOR Value in a Range
en.description:
f returns the element itself for a single element; otherwise, XOR each pair of adjacent elements to get an array one shorter, and recurse until only one value remains. For each query [l,r], find the maximum f value over all non-empty contiguous subarrays within it. Note that f is not an ordinary range XOR.

This site has made the standard input and output explicit; any range not given by the source is marked as this site's protocol.
en.input: The first line contains n q, the second line contains n integers, followed by q lines of 0-based l r, with 0≤l≤r<n. The source gives no size ranges; on this site 1≤n≤2000, 1≤q≤100000, 0≤a[i]≤2³⁰−1.
en.output: For each query, output one line with the maximum value.
en.explanation: Example 1: f of the whole array is 15, which is the maximum, and f of subarray [2,4] is 6, so output 15, 6. Example 2: f of the whole array is 8 xor 8=0, but the adjacent pair [8,1] has f=9, so the maximum is 9, not the ordinary XOR of the three numbers. Example 3: f of a single element is just 0.
hints: Compute f(l,r)=f(l,r−1) xor f(l+1,r) by length. At the same time, best(l,r) is the maximum of f(l,r), best(l,r−1) and best(l+1,r); keep a compact unsigned integer table to answer queries.
